overview: All values in this cursed spirit’s unique row are zero. Its traced action code handles its recovery buff, super attack, and beam effect separately.
technicalOverview: Special Grade Cursed Spirit (CN_090) is a non-playable curse with its own action controller and AI type but only one populated unique row: CharacterUniqueDataTable4/CN_090 at zero-based Id_CharacterUnique index 0, containing fourteen 0.0 floats. The reconstructed CN_090-specific action, AI, effect and homing code does not read that row; its recognizable mechanics are hardcoded in UCN_090_ActionController: a ranged recovery buff on the second Normal 3_1 start, a super-attack focus/event-state sequence, a held and blocked Cursed Energy Attack 2 effect, and ground/air reuse of the same attack sets. The character accessor is a raw UniqueRows[RowIndex]->FloatValue[ValueIndex] dereference with no bounds or null check. Generic fixed-row-0 readers do exist (projection-sorcery restraint fallback, secondary-target steering, and AI hold actions used by another character), but no CN_090-specific caller is established; they are marked unresolved rather than presented as this character's mechanics.

CN_090.title: All-zero single unique row
CN_090.overview: The first Id_CharacterUnique entry is CN_090 in CharacterUniqueDataTable4, so this is zero-based unique row 0. Its remaining entries are None and load as null rows. No direct CN_090 action, AI, effect, projectile, trap or shikigami reader of this row was found; only generic row-0 sites with unproven CN_090 wiring are accounted for below.

0.label: Generic row-0 time/turn fallback
0.simple: The stored value is zero. Nothing in CN_090's own attacks or AI is known to use it. If one of the unwired generic paths ever targets this character, zero would make the projection-sorcery restraint fallback end immediately and would disable secondary-target turning.
0.technical: AGameCharacter::GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue reads UniqueRows[0]->FloatValue[0] without a bounds or null check. Three fixed row-0 read sites were traced. (1) FGameCharacterAction_ProjectionSorceryReceive::Tick uses GetOwnerUniqueFloat(0, 0) only when Request.DamageTableRow is null; otherwise it uses the damage row's RestraintTime. The phase ends when RestraintTime <= ActionElapsedTime, so zero means an immediate end on that tick. (2) UGameCharacterActionController::SteerTowardSecondaryTarget requires a valid secondary target, then uses this value as the divisor of the angle to the target. If it is not greater than 0 (zero here), the out turn time is set to 0 and the function returns before RotateTowardLocation; any positive value would be a degrees-per-turn-time-like divisor, but the source does not establish a physical unit. (3) The CursedEnergyAttack1Hold/2Hold Reset functions use it as the base of a seconds-like Duration, but only CP_040's behavior controller substitutes those hold executors. CN_090 has AIType 22: it gets the dedicated non-playable think node but the default behavior controller, whose CE4/CE5 ordinals are non-hold actions. UCN_090_ActionController::CreateAction and OnHomingWarpEnd contain no unique-float read. Because no reconstructed caller ties these generic reads to CN_090, the character-specific effect remains unresolved.

1.label: Generic CE1 AI hold level scale
1.simple: Zero in the data. Only a generic AI hold action is known to read it, and CN_090 is not wired to that action in the reconstructed source.
1.technical: If FGameCharacterAIAction_CursedEnergyAttack1Hold::Reset runs, Duration = owner unique(0, 0) + owner unique(1, 0) * CursedEnergyLevel. Its Tick adds DeltaTime to Timer and holds the CursedEnergyAttack_1 button while Timer <= Duration, then releases it for a 1-second gap when Timer > 1.0. With this row the level-scaled part is zero. That Hold action is instantiated only by UCP_040_BehaviorController at AI ordinal 0x11; CN_090 AIType 22 falls through to UGameCharacterBehaviorController, whose 0x11 action is FGameCharacterAIAction_CursedEnergyAttack1. The read is real but not established for CN_090.

2.label: Generic CE2 AI hold level scale
2.simple: Zero in the data. Only a generic AI hold action is known to read it, and CN_090 is not wired to that action in the reconstructed source.
2.technical: If FGameCharacterAIAction_CursedEnergyAttack2Hold::Reset runs, Duration = owner unique(0, 0) + owner unique(2, 0) * CursedEnergyLevel. Its Tick adds DeltaTime to Timer and holds the CursedEnergyAttack_2 button while Timer <= Duration, then releases it for a 1-second gap when Timer > 1.0. With this row the level-scaled part is zero. That Hold action is instantiated only by UCP_040_BehaviorController at AI ordinal 0x13; CN_090 AIType 22 falls through to UGameCharacterBehaviorController, whose 0x13 action is FGameCharacterAIAction_CursedEnergyAttack2. The read is real but not established for CN_090.

notes.text: No row-0 camera request belongs to CN_090. MakeUniqueCameraRequest would read row slots 0-10 when CameraMode == 2 (offsets, angle limits, FOV/blend time, easing selector, orbit and roll), but UCN_090_ActionController's CreateAction has no call to it. Reconstructed calls elsewhere pass explicit non-zero rows or a different character's dynamic row. Slots 3-10 are therefore left untraced instead of being given camera meanings.

Trap and shikigami forwarding is not attributed to this row. FGameTrapAction::GetUniqueFloat forwards a value/row pair to the spawner's character interface and generic traps do read row 0 in a couple of places, while shikigami approach code reads owner unique rows through a row parameter. CN_090 has no trap or shikigami row in the authoritative character data, and AGameShikigami's same-named accessor reads the separate ShikigamiUniqueDataTable, so these are not evidence of CN_090 row-0 use.

There is no bounds check, null-row fallback, or sentinel in the accessor. Row 0 exists, but the later None entries in Id_CharacterUnique load as null pointers, so any code asking this character for a higher row would dereference null. A stored zero is just data here, not proof of disuse and not a global 'off' flag.

Second normal hit feeds the super: NormalAttack_3_1 grants BUFF_CURSEDENERGY_RECOVER_INCREASE_CN_090 only when that action's start count is 1. The air NormalAttack_3_1 deliberately looks up the ground Id_AttackSet_Normal_3_1 row, so both forms share the same attack set.

The Super attack is an event-state handoff, not a unique-row tuning block. For non-players its camera can begin only while the super event count is below 1; the first start zeroes cursed energy and adds the owner as a battle focus candidate while that count is <= 0; finishing at start count 1 requests the battle event state and increments the counter, which closes the gate. The air form reuses the ground Super attack-set row.

Cursed Energy Attack 2 controls a projectile-like effect without unique floats: it keeps only effects whose row EffectType is 1, sweeps a capsule from the effect location to the owner's X/Y, disables the effect's damage collision and sets a blocked flag when a shot-blocking hit occurs, then finishes and resets the effect on a later tick. Its attack set is held from the first start; otherwise it chooses H1/H2 sets by cursed-energy level and left-stick down (45.0001 degrees, 0.5 threshold). Verification notes still label the effect's reset tail virtual as unresolved.

AI is specialized but still generic underneath: CharacterDataTable maps CN_090 to AIType 22, which creates FGameCharacterAIThinkNode_CN_090, a NonPlayable leaf with its own think-parameter bands and a Tick that reads the cursed-energy-recovery buff stack. AIType 22 has no case in the behavior-controller switch, so it receives UGameCharacterBehaviorController. Its setup spans level bands 1-3/4-6/7-10 plus states 8 and 9, with distance bands under 800, 800-2000 and 2000-3000.

Control quirks: the controller has no members, refuses tag combos and revival buffs, plays situation voice only for index 1, and requires a full cursed-energy gauge before a cursed-energy technique unless bIgnoreGauge is true. Homing-warp end spawns FX_CP_000_01501 at the waist bone and attaches FX_CP_000_01502 to the mesh root; that same slot-205 body is shared with CP_020 and CP_250 and reads no unique row.

Shared-body caution: CN_090's Super slot-70/130/132 bodies are reused by other controllers, including CN_081. Unique reads beside those copies belong to the other character; for example CN_081's Super beam length comes from its own owner unique (1, 4), not from CN_090's single zero row. CN_090's own CreateAction switch only selects the six customized action classes and otherwise delegates to the base factory.
